description: Fiber optic networks near a Texas address or coordinate: long-haul, middle-mile and metro fiber routes by provider with distance in miles, the nearest carrier hotels, colocation facilities and data centers (PeeringDB-keyed) with distance, and which providers offer fiber-to-the-premises nearby (FCC Broadband Data Collection). Routes are marked by how their path is known: gis_published is the provider's own GIS (real cable path, FiberLight as of March 2022), carrier_on_corridor is a carrier reported on a named highway corridor between two cities (path inferred, not surveyed). Use when someone asks about fiber, connectivity, latency, backhaul or dark fiber for a data center, mining or industrial site, who the carriers are near a tract, or how far a site is from a carrier hotel. Free shows the providers and distances; Pro adds fiber counts, placement (aerial or underground), use (backbone, lateral), status and route names, facility names, and fiber-to-premises locations and speeds. Lit capacity and pricing are not public; this finds who to call.

address.description: Texas street address, e.g. '1201 Main St, Houston, TX'. Use this or lat/lng.

lat.description: Latitude (WGS84). Use with lng instead of address.

limit.description: Provider route groups returned, nearest first. Default 15, max 40.

lng.description: Longitude (WGS84). Use with lat instead of address.

radius_mi.description: Search radius for routes and fiber-to-premises in miles. Default 5, max 25. Facilities are always the nearest ten within 100 miles.

name: fiber_near
title: Fiber near a site
